chapter: Kansas City bands and the Blue Devils
title: Buster Smith and the One O'Clock Jump
summary: Smith brought a trunk of blues music for the Kansas City story; Durham says Smith really did One O'Clock Jump and he and Dan added the trombone parts, earning the nickname Circus Boy.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When we made this Kansas City story, he bought a -- brought a trunk of blues music. And some of that stuff, you never realize it needs to be on the market. I hear from him all the time. We went over some of it, and boy, -- he's the guy that really did The One O'Clock Jump. The score was there, he brought the music, played it off this -- and the other way the other parts got added in was, like, it didn't have nothing to do with the trombones because everybody was hitting the same way and always could come up with something. A guy would say, now, let's see you put something in this, genius. And I'd just start that -- me and Dan, see. Buster made the statement that Dan did it, but it was me and Dan. Of course, it doesn't make any difference,
but that's how he did it. Then they started calling me Circus Boy. There's old Circus.
